Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking the meeting last week. Quick summary of what we need from Redwood to finalize procurement and our security review:

- Dedicated pool hosted in Frankfurt (data residency requirement)
- Initial capacity for Q3: workload profile attached (expected 150k gen tokens/day, 12k embed units/day, peaks up to 2.2k TPS for short windows) — see attachment: Plainsight_Forecast_Q3.xlsx

Appreciate a concise MLP (mutual action plan) we can attach to the procurement package.

Best,

Team / Sam — initial sizing and options below (high level; numbers assume a mixture of M60-equivalent and A100-eq capacity depending on model family). I'll follow up with a CSV cost estimate.

Option A — Conservative (fastest time to provision, lower unit cost):
- 6 dedicated A100-eq GPUs in FRA (sustained)
- Designed for steady-state: covers ~60–70% daily demand; auto-burst to shared pools for short spikes up to 2.5k TPS
- Estimated steady token unit cost (net of committed discount): see attachment runtime-cost-estimate.csv

Option B — Higher-availability (preferred for launches):
- 10 dedicated A100-eq GPUs + 4 hot-warm burst nodes across FR and DE-east (cross-zone)
- Handles sustained load and 3x launch bursts without fallback; recommended if SLA > 99.9% during launches

Operational notes and timeline:
- Provisioning time: 3–4 weeks for reserved capacity in FRA (hardware allocation + infra setup)
- Compliance evidence (SOC2 snapshot we can provide): 5 business days for EU-specific extracts once PO is signed
- Can provide a 30-day warm-up staging pool to validate latency/throughput before SOW goes live

Next steps (proposed MLP for procurement):
1) Mar 4: PO submission (Plainsight)
2) Mar 6: PO confirmed / billing setup completed
3) Mar 10–Mar 31: Provisioning + staging + compliance extract
4) Apr 1: Go-live (soft launch)

If you prefer I can convert Option B into an SOW and provide monthly committed cost with burst pricing + breach/fallback clauses. Deal ID will be DEAL-PLS-2028-0032.
-Karthik

Lina — quick technical notes to feed into the SOW and cost sheet:
- Model family matters: for instruction-tuned LLMs with long context, memory footprint increases KV-cache pressure; that pushes us to slightly larger GPU counts for the same TPS. If Plainsight is using quantized MPT-style models we can reduce GPU needs by ~25% with no noticeable quality regression.
- For burst windows: we recommend a hybrid approach (Option B) plus a 30-day pre-warm where we run replayed traffic to exercise caching / prefix eviction. That reduces cold-start token costs on day 1 of launch by ~40%.
- We will include a line in the SOW about customer-managed KMS and a 2-year audit retention SLA; engineering will provide an EU-only log extraction.

Attached: SOC2-eu-snapshot.pdf (compliance extract) and runtime-cost-estimate.csv (detailed unit math). I'll draft a short-form SOW for Option B and share the Drive link.

—Marissa
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
